notes.claim: In reverse percentage problems the original amount always represents 100%, so after a 5% increase the new amount is 105% of the original.
Finding the original amount before a percentage increase or decrease is called a reverse percentage problem, and works by reversing the change.
A single multiplier can be used to find the original amount after a percentage increase.
Reducing 100 by 20% gives 80, and increasing 80 by 20% gives 96, not 100, because the second 20% is taken of 80, which is 16.

sources.title: Common ways percentages can mislead you - Math Open Reference
sources.quote: For example, if I have 100 items and reduce that by 20% I get 80 items: Now if I increase 80 by 20% I get 96: So I end up with 96 items, not 100.

sources.title: Common ways percentages can mislead you - Math Open Reference
sources.quote: Because in the first percentage I am taking 20% of 100 which is 20. In the second percentage I am taking 20% of 80 which is 16.

sources.title: Percentage change - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Finding the original amount before a percentage increase or decrease has taken place is called a reverse percentage problem.

sources.title: Common ways percentages can mislead you - Math Open Reference
sources.quote: If I increase something by say 20% then reduce it by 20% you might expect to get back to the number you started with.
